constraints: First-stage/day-ahead master problem is mixed-integer linear.
Second-stage/real-time recourse is decomposed into one continuous nonlinear AC subproblem per wind scenario.
Original extensive-form problem is mixed-integer nonlinear and generally intractable.
Wind power production is the only modeled uncertainty.
Wind uncertainty is represented by a finite scenario set.
Use AC network constraints in recourse, including voltage magnitudes, voltage angles, active/reactive line flows, and apparent line-flow limits.
Include unit commitment and dispatch decisions with startup costs in the scheduling stage.
Include real-time reserve deployment, reactive generation, wind spillage, and involuntary active load shedding by scenario.
Include generator active/reactive capacity limits, reserve deployment limits, ramp-up/ramp-down limits, transmission-line capacity limits, and voltage-related AC feasibility constraints.
Scheduled wind power upper bound equals expected wind production.
Apply a heuristic temporal decomposition by relaxing inter-temporal ramping constraints of generating units.
implementation_notes: Formulate as a two-stage stochastic AC unit commitment: first stage = day-ahead market; second stage = real-time operation.
Implement Benders decomposition with MILP master and nonlinear continuous scenario subproblems.
Generate Benders cuts from scenario subproblem solutions and iteratively add them to the master.
Use one subproblem per wind-power scenario; subproblems can be solved independently.
All variables and constants are expressed in per-unit in the paper.
Mathematical definitions of AC line-flow functions are in Appendix A, not present in supplied evidence.
Case study is based on the IEEE one-area Reliability Test System (RTS).
Expected implementation requires both MILP and nonlinear programming solvers.
objective: Minimize expected operating cost for network-constrained stochastic AC unit commitment, including day-ahead commitment/dispatch/startup costs and real-time scenario-dependent recourse penalties/costs such as load shedding and wind spillage.
